claims.statement: Carrier Operations (process owner for pickup scheduling and carrier integration) confirms a correction is possible and reversible, but sets two preconditions: (1) it must run only after the affected carrier feed and its lag are specifically identified, and (2) replaying held allocations is only safe after their pickup slots have been corrected first -- correction must precede replay, not the other way around.
claims.limitation: Tier-1, owner-direct source. This sets the required sequencing and identification step before any mitigation action can be safely proposed.

next_action.rationale: Carrier Operations (c11) requires the affected carrier feed and its lag to be specifically identified before any correction runs, and states the correction is 'limited to a single carrier feed' -- implying more than one feed exists and the fault must be pinned to the right one. Reading partition offsets is the read-only diagnostic that can identify which carrier feed is lagging and by how much, satisfying that precondition. This must happen before apply_slot_correction or replay_held_allocations can be responsibly proposed.
